_description: Host-side CPU contention thresholds for alerts/bsod-risk-prometheusrules.yaml. Two DISTINCT signals since v0.26.0 (peer-review F-02): psi_cpu_waiting_ratio_warn drives BSODRisk_HostCPUContention (real node contention, via Linux PSI), and throttle_ratio_warn drives BSODRisk_VirtLauncherCPUThrottled (a pod capped by its own CPU limit). Source of truth, bound by scripts/ci/validate-shared-thresholds.py.
_why:
N-07 (Wave 7, R-45): check_cpu_overcommit (insights-rules/plugins/bsod_resource_checks.py) reads the K8s pod's DECLARED resource request vs. node capacity -- a scheduling-config heuristic that can read 'fine' while the node is at 100% real contention (over-provisioned requests) or 'overcommitted' while idle (conservative requests). A repo-wide grep for steal/PSI/cpu_pressure/cfs_throttl/noisy neighbor returned zero hits outside that one docstring before this file existed -- there was no signal anywhere for actual, OBSERVED contention. container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total / container_cpu_cfs_periods_total are cAdvisor cgroup counters already scraped by OCP's default monitoring stack (kubelet job) -- no new collection agent, ServiceMonitor, or guest change is required, which is why this is the highest-value, lowest-cost gap the review identified.

F-02 UPDATE (v0.25.0 peer review): the CFS-based alert this file was created for could not fire on a default cluster at all. cAdvisor populates container_cpu_cfs_periods_total / _throttled_periods_total only when the cgroup has a CPU bandwidth quota, and KubeVirt sets requests -- not limits -- on virt-launcher unless the VM specifies resources.limits.cpu or uses dedicatedCpuPlacement. Both sums are therefore 0 on a stock cluster, the ratio is 0/0 -> NaN, and `NaN > 0.25` is false: the alert was SILENT at 100% node contention. Proven with promtool using flat-zero input series. Compounding it, CFS throttling measures a pod exceeding its OWN limit, not node contention -- an oversubscribed node with no limits throttles zero. The expression was kept under an honest name (BSODRisk_VirtLauncherCPUThrottled) and PSI now carries the contention signal.
_units: ratio (throttled CFS periods / total CFS periods over the rate window), 0.0-1.0
_throttle_ratio_warn_note: Sustained CFS throttling above 25% of scheduling periods on a node's virt-launcher pods indicates real CPU contention severe enough to risk guest scheduling-timing BSODs (CLOCK_WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT 0x101, HYPERVISOR_ERROR) on Windows VMs, which are far more sensitive to scheduling jitter than Linux guests.
_calibration_status:
PARTIAL for the run-queue signal (2026-08-19); UNCALIBRATED for the CFS throttle signal.

RUN-QUEUE (BSODRisk_HostCPUContention) -- measured on a live OCP 4.18.26 / CNV 4.18.45 ARO cluster, 3 Intel KubeVirt worker nodes (16 vCPU each), 24h window:
    p50 0.0589   p95 0.2433   p99 0.3049   max 0.4309  tasks queued per CPU
The 1.0 threshold sits 2.3x above the observed peak, and the nodes spent 0% of the window above it. A 0.25 threshold would have spent 4.9% of the window firing.

WHAT THIS ESTABLISHES: the threshold does not false-positive on a lightly-loaded cluster, and the expression returns exactly the KubeVirt nodes (3 of 6) via its label_replace join -- verified on-cluster, which is what allowed the scoping the first implementation had to omit.

WHAT IT DOES NOT ESTABLISH:
  1. That 1.0 CATCHES contention severe enough to bugcheck a Windows guest. No induced-contention run has been done. Absence of an alert on a healthy cluster is not evidence the alert works.
  2. Production representativeness. This cluster's VMs were not even running (their PVCs do not exist), so the measurement is close to an idle floor. A production fleet will sit higher, and the 2.3x margin could shrink.

TO CLOSE: run a stress workload inside a test VM until the node is genuinely contended, confirm the alert fires within its `for:` window and clears afterwards, and record the observed distribution here the way shared/storage-latency-thresholds.json does.

CFS THROTTLE (BSODRisk_VirtLauncherCPUThrottled) -- still UNCALIBRATED (2026-08-04). Separately, its premise was confirmed on the live cluster: 0 of 64 VMs set resources.limits.cpu or dedicatedCpuPlacement, so no virt-launcher pod there would carry a CFS quota and this alert would produce no series at all. That is the F-02 defect, observed in the field.
_runqueue_wait_per_cpu_warn_note:
Average number of tasks queued per CPU on a KubeVirt node, from avg by (instance) (rate(node_schedstat_waiting_seconds_total[5m])). /proc/schedstat's run-queue wait field is the aggregate seconds tasks spent waiting for a CPU, per CPU; rate() makes it seconds-waited per second, and avg by (instance) normalises across the node's CPUs so the value reads as 'tasks queued per CPU'. It is UNBOUNDED above -- unlike a PSI stall fraction, which is 0-1. That distinction is why this is 1.0 and not the 0.25 the first F-02 implementation carried over from the CFS throttle ratio.

WHY NOT PSI: the first implementation used node_pressure_cpu_waiting_seconds_total. It is ABSENT on OCP 4.18.26 / CNV 4.18.45 (ARO) -- no node_pressure_* series exist at all, though node_exporter is running and healthy. Shipping it would have reproduced F-02 exactly: an alert named for a risk it cannot observe. Do not reintroduce PSI without first confirming the series exists on the target platform.

_calibration_observed.cluster: OCP 4.18.26 / CNV 4.18.45, ARO (Azure), 3 Intel KubeVirt workers @ 16 vCPU
_calibration_observed._representativeness_note: Cluster VMs were defined but NOT running (PVCs absent), so this is near an idle floor.
_calibration_observed._psi_note: node_pressure_* returned zero series cluster-wide; node_exporter otherwise healthy (576 node_cpu_seconds_total series).
